_addition_03-09-2026: EGCH was added to the signature list AFTER the list was seeded, and the reason is recorded because a ratchet may otherwise only SHORTEN. IT IS NOT NEW DEBT. EGCH has carried this construction all along; the gate could not SEE it, because the study exposes a reinvestment RATE and no return on capital, and the resolver wanted a return. They are the same statement — rr = g/ROIC — so the return is now derived and EGCH joins the census. AN INSTRUMENT THAT GETS BETTER AT SEEING MUST BE ABLE TO RECORD WHAT IT NEWLY SEES, or improving it makes the build permanently red, which is the check [R-ENF-02] forbids. That is the ONE circumstance in which this list may take a new entry, and it is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a diff.
_ratchet: [R-ENF-02] — knowingly-outstanding work is listed and allowed to fail; the build breaks on a NEW study carrying the construction. THE LIST MAY ONLY EVER SHORTEN (--prune).
_reseeded: 2026-09-03. The gate was first pointed at a NOPAT/W floor and the floor was not the test: of the six studies carrying the g x IC construction only two sit below that floor, so it found the defect on one name and would have missed it on four. The failing test is now the 1/g SIGNATURE, which is exact algebra rather than an estimate. The old breaching group is emptied — removing entries is SHORTENING, the only permitted direction.
_signature: charge = NOPAT x g/ROIC = g x (NOPAT/ROIC), so cycle = IC/charge = 1/g WHENEVER the construction is the reinvestment identity.

signature.ADNOCLS: terminal built on the reinvestment identity: implied cycle 50.0 years against 1/g of 50.0, charging 18.1% of terminal profit. Predates [R-TERM-01]; gets engine/terminal_value.py and a DISCLOSED useful life at its next re-issue. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT MEASURED 03-Sep-2026 AND RECORDED HERE SO THE RE-ISSUE FIXES BOTH: this study's ic_terminal is built as NET BOOK ppe + working capital + intangibles + goodwill (92.5% / 6.9% / 0.6% of 11,439,648), and the reinvestment identity divides g into it. THAT IS NOT A REPLACEMENT-COST INVESTED CAPITAL and two of its three components are not replaced by capex at all — a maintenance programme does not buy back goodwill, and working capital is charged separately as inflation x WC in the corrected construction, so including it here charges for it TWICE. THE SCALE, and the direction is DOWN: the model levies g x IC = 228,793 a year for ever. Book PPE depreciation alone is 612,111 — 2.7x the charge — and book depreciation is struck on HISTORICAL cost, so replacement costs more still. On the disclosed 25-year tanker life applied to GROSS cost, and taking net book at 50-60% of gross for a fleet at this point in its life, maintenance is 705,000-847,000, i.e. 3.1x to 3.7x what the model charges. THE GROSS FIGURE IS NOT IN THIS STUDY'S COMMITTED INPUTS, which is why that is a RANGE off a stated assumption rather than a number: the property, plant and equipment note carries cost and accumulated depreciation and must be sourced at re-issue. AND terminal_value.build() REFUSES this study's inputs as they stand — implied payout 120.2% of terminal NOPAT — because book D&A of 733,379 exceeds IC/25 on the BOOK base. That refusal is the module working: it is telling us the base is wrong, not the life. A further specification point for the same pass: 16.5% of book D&A is RIGHT-OF-USE and investment-property depreciation, and a lease is replaced by paying the lease, not by capex — so the add-back and the maintenance charge must sit on the same asset base. THIS IS THE MODEL REPORT, the document every other study is written against, and it also still carries the typed four-lens blend [R-LENS-03] retired on 02-Sep-2026.
